operations.name: Irving Aarons

expected.charges: Conspiracy arising from the May's Department Store strike; charge changed to coercion on April 1, 1936.
expected.sentence: Held under $1,000 bail during the union prosecution.

updates.prosecutor: William F. X. Geoghan (Brooklyn District Attorney’s office)
updates.indicted: April 1, 1936 — coercion indictment replacing conspiracy charges

operations.research_note: Contemporary April3,1936 Daily Worker p1 identifies Brooklyn DA William F. X. Geoghan responsible for May store strike prosecution and Wednesday coercion indictments naming Aarons, matching existing April1 charge-change account. Hiram Todd is special prosecutor asked to investigate grand-jury conduct, not assumed prosecutor of Aarons. May12 newspaper lists scheduled Special Sessions panel but no completed hearing verified, so judge field left empty. Preserved existing arrest-month, sentence and biography; no custody dates inferred.
